newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says will sign IMF credit deal on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says will sign IMF credit deal on Friday.

text.p: Egypt and the International Monetary Fund will sign on Friday a new standby credit agreement that will persuade international creditors to scrap $4 billion of Egypt's external debt, government newspapers said on Wednesday.

Egypt last week cut tariff rates by up to 25 percent, which economists said was the last of the fund's preconditions to ratify the deal, and the dailies quoted Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid as saying IMF approval was "wholehearted".

"The heads of the IMF and World Bank expressed their support for President Mubarak's policies and our agreement with the fund was total and complete," Obeid told the official Al-Ahram in Washington after he met with fund officials.

The standby credit deal will allow Egypt to withdraw about $200 million annually from the IMF and is sure to persuade its Paris Club creditors to write-off the $4 billion, the third and last tranche of Egypt's official debt that will save the treasury more than $200 million in debt service.

Al-Ahram quoted unnamed IMF officials as saying the new agreement would focus on privatisation, trade liberalisation and restructuring administrative and legal bodies to eliminate long-winded bureaucratic procedures.
Under the credit deal, Egypt would privatise within the next two years about 200 state-owned firms, mainly in the agricultural and industrial sectors.
It would also have to draft a unified investment law, subject of years of parliamentary debate, and implement laws to free imports and exports from bureaucratic hassle.

Arvind Subramanian, the IMF representative in Cairo, told Reuters in August that other reforms outlined in the IMF agreement would promote the private sector, increase efficiency and raise exports to put Egypt "on a higher growth trajectory".
